content.text:
# Review Memo — Garman Software License & Maintenance Agreement (Sparkling as customer)

**Threshold caveat:** Schedules A–F (fees, Specifications, Software description, Authorized Locations, Modifications/data conversion, implementation/training, telephone support) are not attached. They carry most of the commercial risk (price, price escalation, what the software must actually do, support response times). **Do not sign until they are attached, initialled, and reviewed** — Specifications in particular, because the entire warranty (§12), acceptance test (§6) and repair obligation (§10(c)) are measured against them, and §20(j) wipes out any pre-contract representations or RFP responses not captured in them. Add an order-of-precedence clause (Agreement, then Schedules) since §1 says the Schedules "form an integral part."

---

## A. High priority

**1. Perpetuity of the licence is tied to paying all fees forever (§17(a); §12; §17(b)).**
Risk: "remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid" lets Garman argue the licence itself dies if Sparkling stops buying maintenance. §12 also conditions the performance warranty on remaining under maintenance, and §17(b) says Sparkling's only exit requires ceasing use and destroying the Software. Net effect: no ability to drop maintenance without losing the software — permanent lock-in and uncapped renewal pricing exposure.
Fix: separate the licence from maintenance. "The licence granted in §2 is perpetual and irrevocable upon payment of the licence fees set out in Schedule A, and shall not terminate by reason of expiry or termination of Maintenance Services." Add a standalone right for Sparkling to terminate Maintenance Services on 60 days' notice before any renewal without affecting the licence, with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

**2. Termination for payment default can kill the licence (§17(c)(7)).**
Risk: a 30-day cure on a disputed invoice lets Garman terminate a business-critical, perpetual licence.
Fix: Garman's remedy for non-payment is suspension of Maintenance Services only, after 30 days' written notice, and only for undisputed amounts; amounts disputed in good faith are excluded pending resolution. The perpetual licence is not terminable for breach of payment.

**3. Maintenance renewal and pricing are open-ended (§10, §11).**
Risk: "renewable one-year term" — no stated right for Sparkling to renew, no cap on uplift, no end-of-life/end-of-support commitment.
Fix: Sparkling has the unilateral right to renew for at least 5 consecutive annual terms; annual fee increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3–5%, no increase in year 1–2; Garman must give 24 months' notice of any decision to discontinue support (which triggers the §16(b) source code licence).

**4. Support obligations are unenforceable as drafted (§10(b), (c); Schedule F missing).**
Risk: (i) §10(b) contains a material typo — "In the event that the Telephone Support Service **does** provide a resolution … within 2 business days, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services." As written, the repair obligation is triggered only by success. (ii) §10(c) is a bare "best efforts to repair" with no response or resolution times and no remedy for failure.
Fix: correct to "**does not** provide a resolution." Add severity-based response/resolution targets in Schedule F (e.g., Sev 1: 1-hour response, continuous effort, workaround in 8 hours), plus escalating fee credits and a right to terminate Maintenance (with refund of prepaid fees) for chronic failure, without prejudice to the §16(b) source code trigger.

**5. Repair-service exclusions are too broad (§10(c)(1)–(5)).**
Risk: chargeable if Sparkling fails to stay on the current release (forced upgrade treadmill), or if the Software is moved to a "different networking environment or hardware configuration" without consent — which captures ordinary AS/400 hardware refreshes and disaster recovery. "Operator errors" is undefined and easily asserted.
Fix: Garman must support the current release plus the two immediately prior releases for at least 24 months after supersession; Garman's consent is deemed given for like-for-like hardware upgrades, relocation between Authorized Locations, and DR/business-continuity use; delete or narrow "operator errors" to material misuse contrary to the Documentation; Garman bears the burden of proving an exclusion applies.

**6. IP indemnity is materially deficient (§13).**
Risks: (a) the indemnity is limited to "breach of this warranty" — it is not a true third-party infringement indemnity, and there is **no duty to defend** and no obligation to pay third-party judgments/settlements; (b) notice within **10 calendar days** on pain of losing the indemnity; (c) covers only Sparkling and its officers/directors — not affiliates, employees or the Authorized Location entities; (d) the mitigation options in (a)–(c) apply only if use is "enjoined" and there is **no refund/wind-down fallback** if none of them is achievable.
Fix: replace with a standard clause: Garman shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sparkling, its affiliates and their personnel against any third-party claim that the Work infringes or misappropriates IP rights, and pay all damages, costs and settlements; Sparkling to give **prompt** notice, with failure to notify relieving Garman only to the extent of actual material prejudice; Sparkling may participate with its own counsel and no settlement admitting liability or imposing obligations on Sparkling without consent. If none of options (a)–(c) is available within 30 days, Garman refunds all licence and prepaid maintenance fees and reimburses reasonable migration costs. Trigger on any claim or interim injunction, not only a final holding.

**7. Rejection right is the sole remedy for failed software (§7, §8).**
Risk: "in lieu of any other remedy" plus a refund-only unwind. Sparkling absorbs its own implementation, data conversion, training, internal and third-party costs, and 45 business days + 15 business days of delay (≈3 months) before it can even exercise.
Fix: delete "in lieu of any other remedy"; make rejection a right *in addition to* other remedies. On rejection, Garman refunds all amounts paid **plus** reimburses documented out-of-pocket implementation and data-conversion costs (cap negotiable). Shorten cure to 30 calendar days and notice to 10 business days. Add an express obligation on Garman to return all Sparkling data in a documented, machine-readable format at Garman's cost.

**8. Acceptance mechanics are internally inconsistent and create deemed acceptance (§4(a), §6).**
Risks: §4(a) **deems** the existing installations complete and "in good working order" (waiving current defects), and deems Modifications complete at the end of a 60-day period — which conflicts with §6's 30-business-day test and 10-business-day deemed acceptance. §6(a) requires Sparkling to report defects "at the end of each day," giving Garman a waiver argument for anything reported later. §6(c) requires acceptance despite undefined "minor deficiencies."
Fix: (i) redraft §4(a) so existing installations are subject to a one-time 30-business-day verification test, or at minimum carve out latent defects and the §12 warranty; (ii) delete daily notification — notice of deficiencies at any time during the acceptance period and up to 10 business days after; (iii) deemed acceptance only after Garman gives written notice that the period has ended and Sparkling fails to respond within 10 business days; (iv) define "minor deficiency" as one that does not materially affect functionality, is documented on a punch list, and is corrected within 30 days; (v) confirm live production use for a fit-out/parallel run does not constitute acceptance.

**9. Source code escrow / insolvency protection has gaps (§16).**
Risks: (i) §16(b) triggers only on Sparkling's §17(c) termination for Garman default or Garman ceasing to support — it does not clearly cover insolvency alone, receivership, abandonment of the product, or chronic SLA failure; (ii) reliance on **US** Bankruptcy Code §365(n) is misplaced — Garman is a Saskatchewan company; Canadian insolvency law (BIA/CCAA) governs, and §365(n) will likely be unavailable; (iii) the "option to purchase as specified in the Source Code Agreement" refers to an agreement that does not exist; (iv) no verification/audit obligation or remedy if the on-machine deposit goes stale; (v) the release licence does not permit Sparkling's contractors to exercise it on Sparkling's behalf.
Fix: expand triggers (any §17(c)(1)–(6) event, discontinuation/EOL, failure to cure a Sev 1 within X days, assignment of the Software to a third party who does not assume support). Replace/supplement the §365(n) reference: an express, immediate, irrevocable, fully paid-up licence to the Codes granted **now** (with use restricted until a trigger occurs), which is not a contract subject to disclaimer, plus CCAA s.32(6)/BIA s.65.11(7)-style acknowledgement that a disclaimer does not affect Sparkling's use of the licensed IP. Either attach the Source Code Agreement/purchase option (with price) or delete the reference. Add a semi-annual currency certification, Sparkling's right to verify/compile-test, and a right for third-party contractors under NDA to use the Codes for Sparkling.

**10. Limitation of liability — clean up the customer-adverse edges (§15).**
Note: there is no monetary cap (good for Sparkling — resist any vendor attempt to add one, or accept no less than 2–3x annual fees, uncapped for the carve-outs). Problems: "loss of data" is excluded, which is the single most likely harm here (data conversion, on-site access to Sparkling's AS/400s); and "exclusive remedy … shall be the recovery of its direct damages" could be read to bar injunctive relief and the express remedies in §§7, 8, 16(b) and 17(c).
Fix: carve out from the consequential-damages exclusion: loss, corruption or unauthorized disclosure of Sparkling data (or at least the cost of reconstruction/recovery). Add carve-outs to §15 for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, death/personal injury and property damage. Add: "Nothing in this Section limits either party's right to injunctive or other equitable relief, or the express remedies set out in Sections 7, 8, 16(b) and 17(c)."

**11. No assignment/change-of-control flexibility (§3(c), §20(d)).**
Risk: Sparkling (a group holding company in a consolidating industry) cannot assign the licence on a sale, merger or internal reorganization, and cannot move the Software to a new group entity, without Garman's consent — giving Garman a veto and pricing leverage at the worst moment. The affiliate use right in §2 is also limited to affiliates "operating at Authorized Locations."
Fix: permit assignment without consent to (i) an affiliate, and (ii) a successor by merger, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assets/business using the Software, on notice; permit use by newly acquired entities and by third-party outsourcers/IT providers acting for Sparkling's benefit. Conversely, add Sparkling's right to terminate (or to trigger §16(b)) if Garman assigns to a competitor of Sparkling or transfers the Software to a party that does not assume the support obligations.

**12. No data protection, security or "no disabling code" protections (§14 and generally).**
Risk: Garman personnel and Garman-maintained source code sit on Sparkling's production AS/400s; Garman performs data conversion of route/customer records (personal data). The Agreement has no security standards, no breach notification, no restriction on Garman's use of Sparkling data, no confirmation that Sparkling owns its data, no personnel screening, no subcontractor controls, and no prohibition on disabling devices or remote self-help.
Fix: add (i) Sparkling owns all Sparkling data; Garman may use it only to perform its obligations; (ii) reasonable technical/organizational safeguards, prompt breach notification and cooperation; compliance with applicable privacy law; (iii) return/destruction of data on termination; (iv) Garman warrants the Software contains no viruses, malicious code, time-bomb, back door or disabling device, and will not exercise any electronic self-help or disable the Software for any reason.

---

## B. Medium priority

- **§10(a) Software Update Service** — confirm "new releases" includes successor versions/renamed products at no additional licence fee, and that updates will not materially reduce functionality or require Sparkling to purchase new hardware without 12 months' notice.
- **§12 Warranty** — add: Maintenance Services and implementation/training services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by suitably qualified personnel; Software complies with applicable law; Documentation is accurate and sufficient; Garman has disclosed all third-party/open-source components. Also state the warranty remedy (repair, and if not repaired within X days, refund).
- **§13 first paragraph — ownership of Modifications.** Sparkling pays for Schedule D Modifications but Garman owns them, with no exclusivity. At minimum confirm the perpetual licence covers all Modifications at no further fee; consider ownership (or a 12–24 month exclusivity against competing bottled-water/route-delivery operators) for bespoke Modifications Sparkling funds.
- **§14 Confidentiality** — the "required by law" and "professional advisors" items are drafted as exclusions from the definition rather than permitted disclosures, which means the information loses protection entirely. Recast as permitted disclosures with a notice/minimum-disclosure obligation. Add: no obligation of confidence over residuals is implied; return/destruction on request; survival period (indefinite for trade secrets); acknowledgement that injunctive relief is available.
- **§9(b) "best efforts"** — reduce Sparkling's standard to "commercially reasonable efforts"; ensure Sparkling's cooperation obligations do not become a general excuse for Garman's delay (or, if a relief-event concept is added, require prompt written notice and proof of actual impact).
- **§19 Non-solicitation** — this is a **no-hire**, not a non-solicit, and on its face covers *every* Garman employee and binds Sparkling's affiliates group-wide. Narrow to: no active solicitation of the other party's personnel directly involved in the services during the term and 12 months, with carve-outs for general advertising, recruiters not directed at the other party, and unsolicited applicants.
- **§20(f) Force majeure** — no cap. Add: if a force majeure event prevents Garman's performance for more than 30 consecutive days, Sparkling may terminate Maintenance Services with a pro-rata refund and may exercise the §16(b) licence; force majeure does not excuse payment obligations or failures Garman could have avoided with reasonable business continuity measures.
- **§20(h) Jurisdiction** — "non-exclusive" jurisdiction of Nova Scotia means Sparkling can be sued in Saskatchewan. Make Nova Scotia exclusive (or at least exclusive for claims brought against Sparkling), and keep Nova Scotia governing law.
- **§20(a) "Time is of the essence"** — cuts both ways; acceptable only if paired with a cure/materiality qualifier, otherwise any trivial Sparkling delay is a repudiation. Recommend limiting it to Garman's delivery/implementation milestones.
- **Payment terms are absent.** Add net 30–45 days from receipt of a correct invoice; good-faith dispute right (no suspension/termination while disputed); milestone-based payment tied to acceptance (hold back 20–30% of licence and implementation fees until acceptance at all Authorized Locations); interest only on undisputed late amounts; clarify currency (CAD/USD), which party bears GST/PST/withholding, and that Garman bears its own income taxes.
- **No insurance requirement** — add commercial general liability, E&O/tech liability and, if personnel are on site, workers' compensation, with certificates on request.
- **Change control** — no mechanism for scoping/pricing future Modifications, new Authorized Locations or additional services. Add a simple SOW/change-order process with fixed, capped time-and-materials rates (rate card in Schedule A, held for 24–36 months) and an obligation on Garman to make personnel available (§4(b)'s "shall be available for Contracting … as reasonably required" is not an enforceable obligation).
- **Termination transition assistance** — none. Add: on any termination or expiry of Maintenance, Garman will provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 6 months at the Schedule A rates, plus return of Sparkling data in machine-readable form.

---

## C. Drafting errors to correct before signature

| Ref | Issue |
|---|---|
| §2 (p0028) | "safely in executable object code format" — should read "**solely**". |
| §10(b) (p0073) | "does provide a resolution" — should read "does **not** provide". Material. |
| §4(a) (p0041) | Sentences are garbled ("including contracted changes and has been properly installed, is in good working order"; the 60-day Modifications period conflicts with §6). Rewrite. |
| §4(b), §5 | "available for Contracting required installation" / "provide as contracted a qualified personnel" — meaningless as drafted; replace with firm obligations. |
| §6(a) vs §6(d) | "30 business days" vs "30 day period" in §6(b); §6(d) deemed acceptance runs from "completion of the acceptance period" while §6(a) requires daily notice. Harmonize. |
| §14(b) | "already in the rightful possession of **the other party** prior to its receipt from **the other party**" — circular; should be "the receiving party … from the disclosing party". |
| §16(a) | Numbering runs (1)–(5) but (4) and (5) are run together; "Source Code Agreement" is undefined and not attached. |
| §18 | Survival list omits §17(c) (post-termination perpetual licence and refund) and §8; add. |
| §20(b) | Notice by fax/personal delivery only. Add email and courier, with named recipients/titles. |
| Execution block | Undated, no counterparts/authority clause, no schedule initialling. |

---

## D. Bottom line

The two structural problems are **lock-in** (perpetuity conditioned on paying whatever Garman charges for maintenance, warranty conditioned on maintenance, no assignment rights) and **remedy starvation** (rejection as the sole remedy in §7, no duty to defend on IP, no SLA remedies, no repair deadline, loss of data excluded). Items A1–A9 should be treated as conditions to signature; A10–A12 and the Schedule A/D/F content are the next tier. Everything in Section C is a correction Garman should accept without negotiation.

Happy to mark up the document once the Schedules are provided.
